data.turoyo: Naqlawat ste komalimi dawġe me s aǧ ǧirane ste, kowən ġalabe. Hanək ste disa komšaḥnənne w xəlṭənne bayn ḥeṭe diqe, kosaymi qadar dasto, tre, hanək kowən qašye bayn ḥḏoḏe. Bəṯr komanḥtənne w komqawsənne w komnašfənne, bəṯr hanək ste kowən tərxayno, kəmmínale.
data.translation: Manchmal sammelt man auch Ayran von den Nachbarn, sodass eine große Menge zusammenkommt. Man macht ihn Warm, mischt ihn mit gestoßenem Weizen, macht etwa ein zwei Kessel voll, und siewerden dann miteinander steif. Dann nimmt man ihn herunter, schlägt ihn zwischen den Händen und trocknet ihn. Dann wird er zu tirchaino, wie wir es nennen.

rationale: Second Infectum example; wheat-containing dairy mixture and named product extend material coverage of the hand-shaping operation.

rationale: Third Infectum example; filled dough rather than curd, same hand-shaping meaning.
The supplied corpus has šərṭan with emphatic ṭ. The glossary also attests the same food name as šərṭān under šyf (JL 12.14.10). Restore the consonant while retaining the glossary vowel length.

summary: All three tokens instantiate the same ko- Infectum with plural processing agents and indexed material. The hand action is lexical and not expressed by a separate instrument phrase in the Turoyo.
The actual entry has only94/200; the reader's94/240 entry-issue claim is not supported by the supplied entry.94/240 is a genuine additional context.
Do not conflate qws hand-shaping with qwṣ shooting. The inherited etymological doubt remains unchanged; corpus examples establish the operation, not its historical derivation.
Does the verb require repeated patting between the hands or extend to shaping with another technique? The supplied culinary contexts do not decide.
Can the etymology be tied to qose cake shapes rather than the weak inherited qūsā comparison? This run supplies no historical evidence to replace it.
Correct the capitalization of the adjective platte
rationale: Platte modifies Form here and is the adjective platte, not the noun Platte. The sense describes giving the material a flat shape.

summary: Hand-shaping applies to curd, a thickened wheat/dairy mixture and filled dough. Product/material variation does not establish a new verb sense.
